Replace the sh -c execution path with a process API that accepts an argument list and preserves the validated Host as one argument. Validate Host as a supported DNS name or IPv4/IPv6 address in both the Watcher editor and backup-import path, reject shell syntax, whitespace and option-like input, add regression tests, backport the correction, and upgrade to the first fixed release when it becomes available. Until then, do not import untrusted Watcher backups and do not enter untrusted values in Watcher ICMP Host fields.
changes.after: Remove sh -c from the Watcher ICMP execution path. Pass a validated Host as one unchanged element of an argument list to a non-shell process API backed by ProcessBuilder.command(...); never join, quote, or reparse the argument list. Validate Host before storage and immediately before execution in the editor and backup import/restore paths. Add unit, argument-capture, and end-to-end tests that prove rejected values never reach a shell or any process.

Until a vendor-confirmed fixed version is available, disable Watcher ICMP where possible. Otherwise use only reviewed task configuration, do not import untrusted Watcher backups, and remove existing Host values containing whitespace, control characters, option-like prefixes, or shell syntax. These measures reduce exposure but do not remediate the sh -c execution path.

changes.before: Withdrawn Advisory This advisory has been withdrawn because it is a security issue. See https://github.com/micromatch/picomatch/pull/235 issuecomment-6315749381 for more information. This link is maintained to preserve external references. Original Description Picomatch through 4.0.7 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability that allows attackers to block the event loop by supplying single-branch repeated extglob patterns. Attackers can provide globs like +( ) or +( a), which analyzeRepeatedExtglob in lib/parse.js skips, causing exponential backtracking against short crafted strings and denying service to Node.js applications.

changes.before: Converting crafted ISO-2022-CN-EXT input to UTF-8 character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.2 through 2.44 may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash. When the ISO-2022-CN-EXT decoder encounters an invalid input byte sequence like '\x0e' it ends up advancing the pointer tracking the read buffer position twice. If this sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up reading past the bounds of the input buffer. To exploit this, the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

changes.after: Ettercap before 0.8.5.2 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via SSHv1 Dissector

changes.before: Ettercap through 0.8.5.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dissector ssh() in src/dissectors/ec ssh.c that copies a peer-supplied data len without checking remaining packet bytes. A malicious SSHv1 client or server in an intercepted session can send a short packet with a large data len to disclose up to 64 bytes of adjacent heap memory through captured credentials in the interface and log.

changes.before: Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a predictable token generation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access private calendar data by exploiting a missing dateCrea value that causes the md5Id token to collapse to md5(calendarId.userId), both small enumerable integers. Attackers can compute valid tokens and request the misc&action=DisplayIcal endpoint with a forged md5Id to read any user's private calendar events without authentication.
changes.after: Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains a predictable token generation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access private calendar data by exploiting a missing dateCrea value that causes the md5Id token to collapse to md5(calendarId.userId), both small enumerable integers. Attackers can compute valid tokens and request the misc&action=DisplayIcal endpoint with a forged md5Id to read any user's private calendar events without authentication.

changes.before: Omnispace Agora Project 26.10.0 SQL Injection via personsSort Session Value
changes.after: Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 SQL Injection via personsSort Session Value

changes.before: Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated general administrators to inject arbitrary SQL by setting the personsSort session value, which is concatenated unsanitized into ORDER BY clauses in MdlUser.php and MdlSpace.php. Attackers can submit an error-based extractvalue payload through personsSort to leak database information, such as the MariaDB version, via the user and space listing pages.
changes.after: Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated general administrators to inject arbitrary SQL by setting the personsSort session value, which is concatenated unsanitized into ORDER BY clauses in MdlUser.php and MdlSpace.php. Attackers can submit an error-based extractvalue payload through personsSort to leak database information, such as the MariaDB version, via the user and space listing pages.
